articles.title: Analyzing infant cries to detect autism shows potential, but definitive evidence is still lacking
articles.summary: Can a baby’s cry reveal early signs of autism? A new review shows that while certain acoustic patterns and AI tools show promise, there is no definitive evidence yet that autistic infants can be identified solely by crying.

articles.title: AhaBench: Do Agents Learn from Prior Experience? A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Continual Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.05435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern language agents are expected to operate over long horizons: they ask follow-up questions, reuse worked examples, handle tool feedback, and adapt to delayed consequences. Most evaluations still reset the agent after a prompt or score only the final state of one trajectory. AhaBench asks a more operational question: when a fixed model receives useful experience, does its later behavior improve under a related evaluation condition where the obvious support has been removed, changed, or delayed? The suite contains three components. Aha-Puzzle

articles.summary: While childhood intelligence and grades do not predict how people view their memory in old age, a new study finds that early adolescent school anxiety does.

articles.title: Self-perceived romantic desirability is strongly linked to overall self-esteem
articles.summary: People who consider themselves highly desirable romantic partners also tend to report higher overall self-worth. A recent meta-analysis of data from nearly 12,000 individuals confirmed a strong positive association between self-perceived mate value and global self-esteem.

articles.title: Popular brain supplement linked to shorter lifespan in men
articles.summary: A large study involving more than 270,000 people has linked higher blood levels of the amino acid tyrosine to a shorter lifespan in men. Using both observational data and genetic analysis, researchers found that elevated tyrosine could potentially reduce male life expectancy by nearly a year, while no significant effect appeared in women. Tyrosine is found naturally in protein-rich foods and is also sold as a supplement for boosting focus and mental performance, making the finding especially intriguing.

articles.title: The brain’s fuel system rapidly recovers after you stop heavy drinking
articles.summary: Heavy drinking changes how the brain fuels itself. But new research shows this metabolic shift is highly reversible, with the brain’s energy system returning to near-normal within just one month of abstinence.

articles.title: New study reveals how depression twists our perception of fairness
articles.summary: People experiencing depression often view social exchanges through a distorted lens. A new study reveals that depressive symptoms can make unfair financial deals seem more acceptable, but only for those who feel they have high social standing.

articles.title: Psychologists find smartphone screenshots can cause a profound degree of “digital amnesia”
articles.summary: New research reveals that taking a screenshot on your smartphone makes you less likely to remember the image later. Unlike other memory aids, this "digital amnesia" doesn't free up your brainpower for other tasks—it just hurts your memory.

articles.title: Nostalgia for past loves can surprisingly boost current relationship satisfaction
